ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that lines AB and CD intersect at point O, with OE $\perp$ CD. If $\angle AOC = 42^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOC=42^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOD=42^\circ$,\\
since $OE \perp CD$,\\
it follows that $\angle BOE=90^\circ-42^\circ=\boxed{48^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, multiple rays intersect at point O. C, O, D are on the same horizontal straight line, with C on the left and D on the right; A, O, B are on the same oblique straight line, with A at the lower left and B at the upper right; OE extends vertically upward from O and is perpendicular to line CD. Ray OB is located inside the right angle formed by OE and OD. Then reason: It is known that ∠AOC = 42°. Because straight line AB and CD intersect, ∠AOC and ∠BOD are vertical angles, so ∠BOD = 42°. Also because OE ⟂ CD, ∠EOD = 90°. In the figure, OB is inside ∠EOD, therefore ∠BOE = ∠EOD − ∠BOD = 90° − 42° = 48°.
